title: Temporal Weighted Encoding: Towards Maximal-Capacity Spike Coding for ANN–SNN Conversion
claim: Our encoding's representable capacity grows exponentially with timesteps and approximates continuous values finely, while baselines grow linearly with coarse quantization.
layout: 2 panels, side-by-side, log-scale line plot beside staircase approximation plot
description: Two side-by-side matplotlib plots with dashed gridlines, using a red-brown color for the proposed method (TWE) and blue for the baseline (Rate/TTFS). The left panel is a log-scale line plot of number of codings against timesteps 1 to 10. The TWE line with circle markers rises steeply, from about 2 to 10^3. The Rate/TTFS line with triangle markers rises slowly and stays near 10^1. The right panel plots closest encoded value against target value on [0,1]. The blue baseline is a coarse staircase with about 6 levels. The red TWE curve is a fine staircase that hugs the diagonal. Each panel has a legend in the top left. The eye goes first to the diverging lines on the left.
caption: Comparison of encoding capacity and precision. Left: The number of codings available across different timesteps (log scale). TWE achieves an exponential growth of 2T , significantly outperforming the linear growth of rate/TTFS coding. Right: Encoding granularity for values in [0, 1] with t = 6. TWE can approximate continuous values with high fidelity, whereas rate/TTFS coding suffers from coarse quantization steps.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) emulate the spiking behavior of biological neurons and are promising for energy-efficient neuromorphic computing. A widely used strategy to train SNNs is to convert pretrained Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), where the accuracy and efficiency are determined by the spike encoding scheme. Traditional methods based on spike count or timing severely underutilize the available encoding space, leading to large accuracy degradation under low-timestep constraints. More expressive alternatives involve complex dynamics, which hinder scalability and practical deployment. To address these challenges, we propose Temporal Weighted Encoding (TWE). Spikes are implicitly assigned exponentially decaying weights through a recursive integration, drawing an analogy to a temporal bit sequence. We systematically analyze the temporal mismatch caused by this weight pattern and propose temporal relaxation and threshold relaxation to resolve this issue, enabling fast and accurate activation encoding. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TWE achieves negligible conversion loss with significantly fewer timesteps, offering a scalable and efficient solution for SNN deployment.
